File Path: Design Files of TITAN X/top/titan_x_top/titan_x_top.v, Design Files of TITAN X/security/secure_boot/secure_boot.v, Design Files of TITAN X/top/axi_rom/axi_rom.v
Actual Behavior: secure_boot authenticates a hardcoded 59-word test table in envm_image (magic 0x5449544E, 16 payload words 0x10000000..0x1000003C). Upon verification, boot_pass asserts and releases core_rst_n. The core RESET_PC is hardwired to 0x1000_0000, which fetches from u_boot_rom (axi_rom loading firmware.hex). The executed firmware is never authenticated by secure_boot.
Expected Behavior: The hardware Root of Trust must authenticate the exact binary firmware image that the CPU cores fetch and execute from boot ROM prior to releasing core reset.
Root Cause: Architectural decoupling of the authentication datapath (internal envm_image array) from the execution datapath (axi_rom).
Technical Impact: Complete bypass of hardware Root of Trust (CWE-347, CWE-1274). An attacker can supply arbitrary malicious code in firmware.hex; secure_boot will still authenticate the separate envm_image and release the cores to execute unauthenticated malware.
Reproduction Method: Run tb_titan_x_top with an altered firmware.hex; observe boot_pass asserting 1 and CPU executing untrusted instructions without security fault.
Required Correction: Hardware RoT coupled directly to AXI Boot ROM. Pre-boot read port authenticated by secure_boot; AXI fetch interface held locked until boot_pass asserts. Verified in tb_titan_x_top with negative tamper test and CPU instruction retirement.
Required Regression Tests: tb_integ_security_chain, tb_titan_x_top, negative authentication tests with corrupted firmware.hex

Actual Behavior: The authorized NIST P-256 public key (ROT_PUBKEY_QX, ROT_PUBKEY_QY) is hardcoded as an immutable localparam in silicon logic gates with zero in-field key rotation or revocation capability.
Expected Behavior: The root public key should be provisioned via secure one-time programmable (OTP) eFuses or support authenticated key revocation lists.
Root Cause: Root public key trust anchor embedded directly in synthesizable RTL localparam without OTP/eFuse integration.
Technical Impact: Irrevocable trust anchor compromise (CWE-1393). If the root private key is ever compromised, all manufactured silicon devices are permanently compromised with no re-keying mechanism.
Reproduction Method: Static inspection of secure_boot.v lines 38-40; absence of eFuse or OTP macro interface.
Required Correction: Integrated dedicated hardware efuse_ctrl module with OTP bank storage, public key hash registers, and revocation bits. Integrated into secure_boot trust validation.
Required Regression Tests: tb_secure_boot with alternate key provisioning scenarios

Actual Behavior: The boot image header lacks a security version / monotonic anti-rollback counter field, and secure_boot FSM performs no anti-rollback checks.
Expected Behavior: Secure boot should compare the image security version against a hardware monotonic counter in non-volatile memory/eFuses and reject older versions.
Root Cause: Omission of anti-rollback protection from the secure boot specification and header format.
Technical Impact: Vulnerability to firmware downgrade / replay attacks (CWE-1037), allowing attackers to flash older, previously signed firmware containing known exploits.
Reproduction Method: Static code inspection of S_READ_HEADER state in secure_boot.v.
Required Correction: Added 32-bit security version field to boot container header; implemented hardware monotonic counter in secure_boot; verified rollback rejection.

File Path: Design Files of TITAN X/security/secure_boot/secure_boot.v, Design Files of TITAN X/peripherals/sha256_engine/sha256_engine.v
Actual Behavior: sha256_engine performs 64-round compression directly on 16-word blocks without FIPS 180-4 message padding (0x80 byte, zero fill, 64-bit length). secure_boot does not apply padding. Incomplete blocks retain stale data, and standard 2-block padding for 512-bit messages is omitted.
Expected Behavior: Hardware SHA-256 engine or secure_boot controller must perform NIST FIPS 180-4 compliant message preprocessing, padding, and length attachment.
Root Cause: sha256_engine implements raw Davies-Meyer block compression only; software padding was assumed but never implemented in secure_boot FSM.
Technical Impact: Cryptographic non-compliance with standard tools (OpenSSL, Python hashlib). Hashes calculated by standard toolchains fail verification in hardware unless custom unpadded compression is used.
Reproduction Method: Compute standard SHA-256 on 16-word payload using Python hashlib; compare with hardware computed_hash in tb_sha256_engine.
Required Correction: Implemented full NIST FIPS 180-4 padding (0x80 delimiter, big-endian length attachment, zero fill) in secure_boot FSM. Validated against standard hashlib SHA-256 vectors.
Required Regression Tests: tb_sha256_engine against NIST CAVP test vectors with non-block-aligned lengths

Actual Behavior: ecdsa_engine implements 256-bit modular multiplication (x * y) and 512-bit modulo division (% P_256) as combinational Verilog functions. In S_STRAUS, up to 26 cascaded 256-bit multipliers and dividers are chained in a single clock cycle.
Expected Behavior: Complex elliptic curve field arithmetic must use iterative multicycle Montgomery multipliers or dedicated DSP/math coprocessor cores.
Root Cause: Behavioral algorithmic modeling used in place of synthesizable hardware arithmetic architectures.
Technical Impact: Complete failure of synthesis timing closure at target SoC frequencies (50-200 MHz); causes logic synthesis tools (Yosys) to hang during elaboration; physically un-routable.
Reproduction Method: Attempt synthesis of ecdsa_engine in Yosys; observe extreme memory and CPU stall or timing paths exceeding 100+ ns.
Required Correction: Implemented synthesizable iterative multicycle Montgomery multiplier mont_mul_256 (256 cycles/mult) with FAST_SIM accelerated verification mode. Clean Yosys elaboration and timing.
Required Regression Tests: Synthesis timing check and tb_ecdsa_engine latency validation

Actual Behavior: psel_uart0 uses aperture match (paddr[31:16] == 16'h4001). This matches all addresses from 0x4001_0000 to 0x4001_FFFF, colliding with RTC, GPIO, WDT, SPI, I2C, CLINT alias, SD/MMC, QSPI, and VDMA. Writes update UART0 and the peripheral simultaneously. Reads always return UART0 data due to priority in prdata_mux.
Expected Behavior: psel_uart0 must decode strictly its allocated 4KB window (paddr[31:12] == 20'h40000 || paddr[31:12] == 20'h10000).
Root Cause: Erroneous 16-bit prefix match (16'h4001) introduced in APB decoder.
Technical Impact: Fatal system-level peripheral failure. CPU cannot read status or data from RTC, GPIO, WDT, SPI, I2C, SD/MMC, QSPI, or VDMA. Any write to these peripherals corrupts UART0 configuration.
Reproduction Method: Execute an APB read to GPIO (0x4001_1000) or RTC (0x4001_0000) via top-level interconnect; observe returned data matches UART0 registers instead of the peripheral.
Affected Modules: titan_x_top, apb_bridge, uart_16550, gpio_ctrl, rtc, watchdog_timer, spi_master, i2c_master, mmc_controller, qspi_controller, vdma
Required Correction: Corrected psel_uart0 to strict 4KB window 0x4000_0000 (and legacy 0x1000_0000); de-mocked tb_integ_peripheral_bus with 28 apertures; verified complete peripheral isolation without cross-corruption.
Required Regression Tests: Top-level bus regression reading and writing every individual APB peripheral

Actual Behavior: Watchdog timer output wdt_reset_n is connected to an internal wire with zero sinks; it does not connect to core_rst_n, reset_sync, or any reset tree logic.
Expected Behavior: Watchdog timeout assertion of wdt_reset_n must trigger a hardware core or SoC reset to recover from deadlocks or software lockups.
Root Cause: Floating net; reset controller integration was never completed in top-level RTL.
Technical Impact: Loss of watchdog hardware recovery. If the CPU enters an infinite loop with interrupts disabled or suffers a bus deadlock, the system is unrecoverable without external power-cycle.
Reproduction Method: Grep wdt_reset_n in titan_x_top.v; observe it is only declared and connected to u_wdt output.
Required Correction: Integrated wdt_reset_n into core_rst_n generation (core_rst_n = rst_n & boot_pass & wdt_reset_n). Verified in tb_titan_x_top with active watchdog reset injection and recovery.
Required Regression Tests: tb_watchdog_timer integration test verifying core reset on timeout

File Path: Design Files of TITAN X/includes/params.vh, Design Files of TITAN X/memory/l2_cache_top/l2_cache_top.v, Design Files of TITAN X/top/titan_x_top/titan_x_top.v
Actual Behavior: titan_x_top instantiates l2_cache_top without parameter overrides, falling back to SETS=64. The actual elaborated L2 cache is 16 ways * 64 sets * 64 bytes = 64 KB, despite claims and params.vh declaring 2048 sets (2 MB).
Expected Behavior: Top-level L2 cache instance should propagate params.vh configuration or documentation must be corrected to reflect actual 64 KB capacity.
Root Cause: Parameter macro L2_SETS not passed to l2_cache_top instantiation in titan_x_top.v.
Technical Impact: Severe multicore cache thrashing and memory latency degradation (32x smaller cache than documented); invalidates all architectural performance projections.
Reproduction Method: Inspect instantiated parameters of u_l2_cache in titan_x_top.v; calculate 16 * 64 * 64 = 65536 bytes.
Required Correction: Propagated L2 cache parameters and aligned architectural documentation with physical macro allocation.
Required Regression Tests: Elaboration check and cache capacity benchmarks in tb_l2_cache_top

File Path: Design Files of TITAN X/memory/l2_cache_ctrl/l2_cache_ctrl.v, Design Files of TITAN X/memory/l2_data_array/l2_data_array.v
Actual Behavior: l2_cache_ctrl implements data_mem and tag_mem as flat behavioral flip-flop arrays (over 550,000 FFs for 64 KB; over 16 million FFs for 2 MB). The foundry SRAM macros (sram_32x64_180nm, sram_512kx8_180nm) and wrapper l2_data_array are completely unintegrated.
Expected Behavior: L2 data and tag arrays must instantiate foundry compiled SRAM macros for density, timing, and power feasibility.
Root Cause: SRAM macro integration was abandoned in favor of behavioral flip-flops during controller debugging.
Technical Impact: Massive silicon area bloat, extreme power dissipation, and inability to synthesize a 2 MB cache without synthesis memory exhaustion.
Reproduction Method: Inspect data_mem declaration in l2_cache_ctrl.v; check synthesis cell reports showing standard cell DFFs instead of SRAM macros.
Required Correction: Integrated compiled foundry synchronous SRAM macros sram_32x64_180nm via l2_data_array with 1-cycle read latency support. Verified in Yosys synthesis cell accounting.
Required Regression Tests: Synthesis area report and tb_l2_cache_top timing qualification

Actual Behavior: The processor implements RV64IM_Zicsr Machine-mode only. Floating-point (F/D) is tied off, Atomics (A) is tied to 0, Compressed (C) traps as illegal, Supervisor mode (S-mode) and User mode (U-mode) are absent (MPP hardwired to 2'b11), and Sv39 MMU is unintegrated (mmu_ptw_arvalid=0).
Expected Behavior: Processor implementation must match the claimed RV64GC Linux-capable specification or project specification must be formally revised.
Root Cause: Subsystems (FPU, MMU, AMO, S-mode CSRs) were left unintegrated or stubbed during development.
Technical Impact: Impossibility of running Linux or any OS requiring virtual memory and user privilege isolation. Binary incompatibility with standard RV64GC Linux distributions.
Reproduction Method: Inspect rv_csr.v (mstatus MPP, misa); attempt to execute c.addi or lr.w; observe illegal instruction trap.
Required Correction: Formally reconciled ISA specification to RV64IM_Zicsr; integrated and verified rv_fpu and rv_mmu modules; validated Machine-mode execution suite.

Actual Behavior: 18 synthesizable RTL modules (rv_mmu, rv_ptw, rv_tlb, rv_fpu, l2_data_array, l2_tag_array, l2_snoop_filter, aes_engine, can_controller, qspi_controller, mipi_csi2_rx, isp_pipeline, hdmi_ctrl, interconnect_mpu, qos_controller, sram macros, envm_ctrl) are completely disconnected from the top-level SoC.

Technical Impact: Over 35% of the repository RTL is dead code; features claimed in marketing/architecture documents do not exist in the synthesized bitstream.
Reproduction Method: Cross-reference module hierarchy with instance pins in titan_x_top.v.
Required Correction: Wired all 18 previously disconnected modules into titan_x_top.v; elaborated full 79-module design in Yosys with 0 unmapped blackboxes.
Required Regression Tests: Full SoC elaboration and interconnect boundary testing

File Path: Design Files of TITAN X/interconnect/axi4_crossbar/axi4_crossbar.v, Design Files of TITAN X/top/titan_x_top/titan_x_top.v
Actual Behavior: axi4_crossbar routes 0x0000_0000..0x0FFF_FFFF to Slave 3 (documented as Low Memory / SRAM). However, titan_x_top groups Slave 3 into gen_unused_axis and connects it to a hardwired DECERR generator (returning 0xDEAD_DEAD_DEAD_DEAD and 2'b11).
Expected Behavior: Slave 3 should connect to on-chip SRAM (axi_sram.v) or unmapped crossbar accesses should route to T_UNMAPPED.
Root Cause: Omission of on-chip SRAM instance on crossbar Slave 3 port in top-level netlist.
Technical Impact: Any processor access to addresses below 0x1000_0000 results in DECERR bus fault; claimed on-chip scratchpad SRAM is non-existent.
Reproduction Method: Initiate AXI read to address 0x0000_1000; observe DECERR response and dead data.
Required Correction: Instantiated 64KB on-chip axi_sram on crossbar Slave 3 port (0x0000_0000..0x01FF_FFFF). Verified memory reads/writes in tb_integ_memory_hierarchy.

Actual Behavior: Top-level SoC testbench tb_titan_x_top performs zero instruction execution, zero memory reads/writes, and zero peripheral accesses. It only checks whether clock/reset pins are not X, waits 1000 cycles, and unconditionally prints 'PASS — All integration checks passed'.
Expected Behavior: Top-level testbench must execute end-to-end boot code, verify CPU instruction retirement, memory subsystem traffic, and peripheral register accesses.
Root Cause: Testbench written as a pin-activity smoke test rather than a functional verification suite.
Technical Impact: False sense of verification qualification. Critical bugs (DEF-SEC-01, DEF-ARCH-01, DEF-ARCH-02) were completely missed despite claims of 100% test pass rate.
Reproduction Method: Inspect tb_titan_x_top.v lines 120-172; observe absence of any bus assertions, instruction checks, or peripheral transactions.
Required Correction: Replaced vacuous delay with genuine Core 0 instruction execution and writeback retirement checks (wb_we && wb_rd != 0). Verified 6 retired instructions, arithmetic writebacks, and UART0 MMU accesses.

Actual Behavior: Integration testbench tb_integ_peripheral_bus does not instantiate titan_x_top; instead, it instantiates axi4_to_ahb, uart_16550, and rtc directly, and writes its own mocked APB decoder. Because it mocked the decoder, it masked the critical DEF-ARCH-01 bug in titan_x_top.v.
Expected Behavior: Integration testbenches must test the actual synthesized RTL netlist or top-level hierarchy without mocking critical interconnect logic.
Root Cause: Testbench author recreated the decoder locally rather than connecting to the SoC top-level decoder.

Required Correction: Replaced mocked 2-line decoder with genuine 28-aperture APB decoder matching titan_x_top.v; added instances of gpio_ctrl and watchdog_timer; fixed zero wait-state combinational prdata; verified 9 tests pass.
